newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, APRIL 28-SUNDAY, MAY 4.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, APRIL 28-SUNDAY, MAY 4.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
LUXEMBOURG - EU justice and home affairs ministers meet. Discussions focus on a report on organised crime to be presented to the Amsterdam European Council (Monday).

LUXEMBOURG - EU foreign ministers meet (Monday-Tuesday). Discussions focus on relations with Iran and Turkey, preparations by Poland and Hungary to join the EU, inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms.

THE HAGUE - Dutch Social and Economic Council holds forum on "The future of the social dialogue at Community level" (Monday-Tuesday). Social and Economic Council President Klaas de Vries holds press briefing, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok addresses the conference participants at a dinner (Monday).
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting.
* Thursday - EU institutions closed for Labour Day.
* Thursday-British elections.
MONDAY, APRIL 28
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU justice and home affairs ministers meet (1430/1230 GMT). Discussions focus on a report on organised crime to be presented to the Amsterdam European Council.

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Commission hosts "European cohesion forum" (1430/1230 GMT) (to Wednesday). Discussions focus on the upcoming reform of the EU's structural funds, the EU's achievements in improving social and economic cohesion and possible improvements for the future. Speakers include: European Commission President Santer, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles, Committee of the Regions President Pasquall Maragall, ECOSOC President Tom Jenkins, European Commissioners Wulf-Mathies, Flynn and Fischler. Venue: Palais des Congres. Contact: Mr Scheins (322) 295 1409.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission hosts conference on "The new computerised transit system" uniting EU officials, economic operators and national authorities from 31 European countries. The conference will present the new system for tracking goods subject to customs duties that are transported across the EU.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin holds news conference on the outcome of his meeting at NATO (1230/1030 GMT). Venue: NATO. Contact: Romanian Liaison Mission to NATO (322) 707 3617.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - World Customs Organisation holds forum on "Reshaping customs - a strategic outlook" (0930/0730 GMT) (to Wednesday). Contact: Francoise Le Grand by fax (322) 508 4241.
LEUVEN, Belgium (NEW ITEM) - Leuven Catholic University, Law Faculty, holds news conference on "Working time developments in Europe" (1645/1445 GMT). Venue: Law Faculty (32) 16 32 52 02.

THE HAGUE (NEW ITEM) - Dutch Social and Economic Council holds forum on "The future of the social dialogue at Community level" (and Tuesday). Social and Economic Council President Klaas de Vries holds press briefing at 1130/0930 GMT. Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok addresses the conference participants at a dinner at the Kurhaus, Scheveningen, at 2000/1800 GMT. Speakers include: Dutch Employment and Social Affairs Minister Ad Melkert and European Commission Directorate-General V (Social Affairs) Director General Allan Larsson. Venue: Congress Centre. Contact: Dutch Social and Economic Council (31) 70 3 499 499.
TUESDAY, APRIL 29
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU foreign ministers meet (and Tuesday).
Agenda includes:
- (0930/0730 GMT) EU position for Association Council with Poland.
- EU position for Association Council with Hungary.
- Trade issues:
- Community preferential trade agreements;
- Textile imports (EC regulation 3030/93).
- (possibly) Live bovine imports.
- Transatlantic relations.
- Switzerland.
- Mediterranean policy: Malta Euro-Med Conference April 15-16.
- Racism and xenophobia monitoring centre.
- EU position for Association Council with Turkey.
- Situation in former Yugoslavia, Belarus, Iran and Great Lakes Regions.
- Middle East peace process.
- Commission presentation on Hong Kong.
- (1330/1130 GMT) Signature ceremonies with Laos and Cambodia.
- (1600/1400 GMT) Inter-governmental conference (IGC) ministerial meeting; EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles attends.
- (1830/1630 GMT) Signature ceremony with Former Yugoslavian Republic of Macedonia.
- (1900/1700 GMT) Association Council with Turkey followed by dinner.
BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds conference on "Vertical restraints green paper: does it meet business needs?" (0900/0700 GMT). Venue: Radisson SAS Hotel.

BRUSSELS - Centre for Economic Policy Research and ECARE (European Studies Institute, Free University of Brussels) hold joint lunchtime meeting on "EMU: getting the end-game right" (1330/1130 GMT). Venue: ECARE, 39 avenue Franklin Roosevelt. Contact: Nancy De Munck, ECARE (322) 650 3075.
BRUSSELS - The Philip Morris Institute (PMI) holds conference on "World trade policy for the 21st century - Delivering the goods after Singapore". Contact: PMI (322) 732 1156.
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 30
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU foreign ministers meeting continues.
Agenda includes:
- (0930/0730 GMT) Inter-governmental conference (IGC) resumes - followed by lunch
- (1500/1300 GMT) Association Council with Poland.
- (1630/1430 GMT) Association Council with Hungary.
- (1830/1630 GMT) Dinner with Hungary and Poland.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0700 GMT).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner Liikanen communication on draft budget for 1998.
- Commissioner Van Miert, Bangemann, Monti communication on the implementation of Commission decision of December 18, 1996, on the granting of concessions in the telecoms sector.
- Commissioners Monti and Gradin action plan for transit in Europe - new customs policy.
- Commission President Santer and Commissioner Monti action plan for the single market.
- Commission President Santer and Commissioners Bonino, Bangemann, Flynn, Cresson and Monti communication on control and scientific consultation in food safety.
- Commissioners Cresson and Flynn report on access to continuing training in the EU.
THURSDAY, MAY 1
- EU institutions closed for Labour Day.
- British elections.
FRIDAY, MAY 2
No events scheduled.
SATURDAY, MAY 3
No events scheduled.
SUNDAY, MAY 4
No events scheduled.
